description: Consortis Geospatial publishes this GPL-3.0 QGIS plugin to inspect disconnected pieces in road-network line layers. A user selects a vector layer and a maximum length. The plugin then uses a spatial index to flag short segments whose endpoints do not connect, lists them in a dock panel and highlights them on the map. The public GitHub repository contains Python plugin files and installation instructions; no road dataset or precomputed results are supplied. The code is free under GPL-3.0. A modeller could check a road topology before assigning traffic flows or simulating disruptions, because isolated segments can create false routes and components. The checker uses the spatial coverage and data currency of the input layer; it has no fixed place or time of its own. This review did not install QGIS, execute the plugin or test large networks. The README links to a differently named issue repository, so support history is uncertain. Related resources are the user-provided road networks to be checked.
